title: Life on the West Coast compared with the East
summary: He describes cheap homey living in Los Angeles, a $38 furnished apartment, and his marriage to Freddie Washington.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: You mentioned you were working again with Les Hite and Lionel Hampton.
-- what, when you went back with the Cotton Club?

Yes. See, you can't hardly imagine, unless you're a very old person, the atmosphere in those clubs at the time. We had a terrific atmosphere amongst the different bands, the different musicians, the studios and the bands. Oh, everything that went on in the music business in those days was really terrific. And the western part of the country had a complete different atmosphere than the eastern part, I found out when I left. It was real homey out west. It was a beautiful atmosphere out here. Things were reasonable, things were cheap.
For instance, to show you what I mean. I had a three room apartment in L. A., new, completely furnished. We had
everything in there from -- well, just everything, clear down to dishtowels and a dozen of these, a dozen bath towels, a dozen of this. Everything, light and gas, paid. $38.00 a month.
'34, '35. Let's see -- and that's just before the war started developing.
Still during the Depression years? That's sort of the end of the Depression?

Sort of the end of the Depression, yes. Because by this time I had gone East and gotten married. I had married this girl, Freddie Washington, that did one of the lead roles in "Imitation of Life." And that was the apartment that we had in California. So everything was so nice then. You never heard anything like three and four hundred dollars a month for a one room, bedroom. So it was really nice, really beautiful out here.
